messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert: API Gateway -> elevated 502/504 rate detected for /v1/generate across edge-pop-03 and edge-pop-07. Error rate: 18% 5xx over 5m. Paging @oncall-sre (jordan).

jordan: acked. jumping in. pinging @lee for edge-proxy logs and @sam for routing config.

lee: on it. seeing a sharp rise in `upstream_reset` and `response_timeout` from edge-pop-03 around 02:14 UTC. sample logs:
```
[02:14:22] envoy upstream_reset: stream reset by peer, op=RESET
[02:14:24] cluster upstream response_timeout after 15s
```

maria: product-ops flagged a customer-facing alert — a handful of high-traffic customers reported failed requests. impact note: some streaming calls are failing mid-stream.

sam: quick hypothesis: control-plane pushed new route weight to a canary pool at 02:11 that might be saturating a smaller backend set. checking rollout history...

lee: confirmed — rollout id `cana-2026-07-08-02` adjusted weight to canary=30%. canary hosts are on smaller gpu nodes and upstream latencies spiked.

jordan: ok let's triage steps: 1) reduce canary weight to 0% or pause rollout, 2) enable circuit-breaker at edge for that cluster, 3) scale canary if needed, 4) rollback if errors persist.

sam: reducing canary weight to 0 now. command posted to control plane: `rdctl rollout set-weight cana-2026-07-08-02 0`

incident-bot: Action recorded: rollout weight updated by sam at 02:18 UTC.

lee: after weight ->0, 502 rate dropped from 18% -> 7% in ~90s. still above baseline (0.5%). seeing persistent tail in edge-pop-07.

maria: customer-impact summary: 9 customers with >2% failed requests, 3 with >10% (internal list redacted). product-ops recommends we open incident ticket and prepare status update.

kaia: suggesting temporary circuit-breaker config on edge cluster to reject new requests to canary backend after queue depth > 100 and 5xx > 5% for 2m. I can push a short-lived override.

jordan: do it. push only to edge-pop-07 first. keep monitors in place.

kaia: pushing envoy override now: `envoyctl set-cluster-config edge-pop-07 cluster.canary upstream.max_connections=100 circuit_breakers.threshold=5percent`

lee: override applied. post-change metrics: edges-pop-07 5xx dropped to 2% after 45s. overall platform 5xx at 3.1%.

sam: given the canary pool size and oob errors, I'm going to scale canary nodes by +2 (temp) while we sort the image. `k scale deployment canary-backend --replicas +2`

incident-bot: Autoscaling event: canary-backend scaled from 3 -> 5 by sam at 02:25 UTC.

jordan: good. next: correlate app logs for OOMs or queue stalls. @lee can you grab a flamegraph / heap histogram for canary instance 5a3b?

lee: pulling stack, looks like a backlog in the request processing loop — many requests blocked on external cache (redis) timeouts. sample trace: `redis timeout 500ms -> request queue buildup`.

maria: product-ops — is redis cluster healthy? any recent deploys?

sam: redis cluster reported higher latencies in the same window due to a maintenance task on shard-2. ops team disabled compaction mid-window (was scheduled), that might have coincided. contacting infra.

kaia: mitigation summary so far: 1) rolled canary weight back to 0% 2) applied circuit-breaker on affected edge-pop 3) scaled canary pool 4) autoscaling + temporarily rerouted traffic to stable pool.

jordan: traffic leveled off. 502s now at 0.6% overall. still monitoring for recurrence for next 15m. setting incident severity to P1 for follow-up and customer comms.

product-ops: drafting customer note. will send a short update in 10m. please use the incident ticket `INC-2026-482` for follow-ups.

lee: quick note: we saw a single recent deploy to canary-backend at 02:07 that added a new cache pattern. tagging `deploy 0f3a2b` as potential contributing factor.

sam: to be safe, I'm preparing a rollback of that deploy if errors persist after infra compaction finishes. rollback command staged: `rdctl deploy rollback canary-backend 0f3a2b` (requires approval).

jordan: ok hold rollback for now — infra is addressing redis shard compaction. if latencies subside in 10m we'll avoid rollback. keep me posted.

incident-bot: Note: oncall handoff scheduled. @jordan will hand off to @kaia in 90 minutes for monitoring and post-incident follow-up.

kaia: I'm taking the 02:30-05:30 shift. will own postmortem and coordinate with infra for redis scheduling changes.

maria: customer-ops will send out the outbound: brief explanation + ETA for full root cause analysis.

jordan: thanks team. immediate mitigation worked. next actions: - infra to finish compaction + confirm redis latency baseline - eng to run stress test on canary-backend with cache failures - product-ops to publish customer note and status page update - ops to review scheduled maint windows and add guardrails.

sam: logging follow-up created: `ENG-4987` for investigating `deploy 0f3a2b` cache pattern.

kaia: I'll own the postmortem doc and include a runbook update: add circuit-breaker thresholds for canary weight changes and enforce canary pool minimum size.

jordan: handing off now to kaia. :white_check_mark: Thanks everyone for the quick cooperation.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: P1 -> open. Handoff: jordan -> kaia at 02:30 UTC.

kaia: acknowledged, taking over. I'll post the postmortem link when it's ready and keep the incident ticket updated. :memo:
